messages:
sasha: Hey team - noticed a weird p95 uplift in APAC yesterday after we flipped the default kernel from Triton-vendor -> flashv3 for q8 models on H100. Thought it was transient but looks reproducible in our small-batch, long-sequence workload. :thinking_face:

maria: Do you have numbers? small-batch = batch size 1-2, long-seq = 1024-2048 tokens right?

sasha: Yep. Baseline (vendor-triton): p95=92ms, p99=170ms. After switch to flashv3 q8: p95=128ms, p99=260ms. Throughput steady but tail worse. Ran in ap-northeast-1 on H100s.

ben: That's a pretty big tail shift. Could be packing/warp divergence or small-batch kernel overhead. Any change in kernel warmup/waves?

sasha: We instrumented KV cache hits and saw more GPU kernel launches per request with flashv3 for short batches due to different packing heuristic. Also saw increased small kernel launch variance in perf counters.

kai: Might be scheduling on multi-tenant host -> GPU context preemption? But vendor kernel had similar environment. Did the GPU driver or CUDA version change in the rollout?

sasha: No driver changes. We only changed the runtime kernel selection policy to prefer flashv3 for fast-path. Canary applied to apac only.

maria: Could this be quantization-related (q8) interaction with flashv3 codepath? Maybe extra dequant/requant steps for attention that cost us for long sequences. Any microbench of pure attention kernel for seq=2048?

sasha: Ran a microbench on a dedicated node: flashv3 attention kernel latency for seq=2048 was ~75ms vs vendor 62ms. The diff grows with sequence length. For short sequences (<512) flashv3 still wins for throughput but not for our small-batch long-seq tail.

devon: Two hypotheses: 1) flashv3's tiling causes uneven occupancy on H100 for very long seqs in q8, 2) Triton's fused kernel/algorithms have a better tail-case for these shapes. We should run kernel-level traces (nvtx, CUPTI) and compare occupancy/warp stalls.

ben: Agreed. Also run with continuous batching disabled to isolate batching heuristics. If automatic packing fires differently between kernels it could add latency jitter.

sasha: I ran a config sweep: 
```
./bench --model my-prod-q8 --kernel flashv3 --batching off --seq 2048 --runs 200
# p95 ~130ms
./bench --model my-prod-q8 --kernel triton-vendor --batching off --seq 2048 --runs 200
# p95 ~95ms
```
So it's not autoscaler/packing only.

kai: Interesting — what about mixed-precision math path or different cuBLAS/cuDNN involvement? flashv3 may fallback some ops to cuBLAS for long sequences which could cause queueing. Check GPU timelines for long GEMM ops.

sasha: CUPTI timeline shows longer GEMM kernels in flashv3 path and occasional preemption spikes aligning with p99.

maria: For risk mitigation: let's pause APAC-wide switch and revert APAC to vendor kernel default while we root-cause. Keep EU/US on flashv3 if they are fine. Add a gating rule: only flip for payload shapes where flashv3 improves p95 AND p99 by at least 5% (safety margin).

devon: Agreed. Also propose building a small automated shaped benchmark suite for onboarding that covers: small-batch long-seq, small-batch short-seq, large-batch short-seq across A100/H100/L40 in each region. We can run this suite pre-rollout and block if tail regresses >10%.

ben: I can add that to the model onboarding CI. Will include a `kernel-switch` job that runs the shaped benchmarks and uploads a summary to the console. Example check: 
```json
{ "shape": "small-batch-longseq", "metric": "p95", "baseline": 92, "candidate": 128, "delta_pct": 39 }
```
If delta_pct > 10 fail the job.

maria: Ops question: do we need to add hysteresis to selector so we don't flip back-and-forth during transient infra noise? e.g., require 1 hour stable improvement + no p99 regression >5% over 24h.

devon: Yes. Add hysteresis + cooldown (24h) and a canary progressive rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) per-region. Also add automatic fallback to vendor if p99 exceeds threshold.

sasha: I'll rollback APAC now and start the kernel-level traces on a dedicated H100 node. Uploading logs to https://console/internal/bench/2563 and will tag relevant runs. :eyes:

kai: When you have CUPTI traces, ping me. I'll correlate with host-level preemption logs and MIG/SM utilization.

sasha: Plan summary: revert APAC default -> run kernel traces -> run shaped bench suite across A100/H100/L40 -> add kernel-switch CI gating + hysteresis + staged rollout. Target: complete analysis and new rollout policy by EOW.

maria: Thanks. Good catch. Also add a note to the release playbook so PMs know we reverted APAC and why.

opsbot: Automated action: APAC default kernel rolled back to triton-vendor at 2563001500 by opsbot. Incident ticket: #INF-4921 created.

ben: I'll start on the CI job today. Sasha, once you upload traces I'll triage the kernel-level diff and propose micro-optimizations or fallback heuristics.

sasha: Thanks all. Will post the first trace link in this thread when available. :thumbsup:
